mainTopic: Walking on the altar ramp, and how bird offerings (חטאת העוף and עולת העוף) are performed and disqualified
overview: The amud opens at the end of a discussion about the כהן גדול pouring wine. He walked around the altar empty-handed, and רבא proves this from the wording of the משנה. A ברייתא then explains which side of the ramp people use to go up and come down. The גמרא wrestles with its use of 'right' and 'left': רבינא changes the wording, while רבא's two-viewpoint answer ends with a קשיא. Next, a משנה describes the חטאת העוף: מליקה without separating the head, blood sprinkled on the lower wall of the מזבח, and the meat eaten by the כהנים. The גמרא proves the lower wall from the פסוק 'יִמָּצֵה'. It then describes how the כהן grips the bird for מליקה, one of the hardest services in the מקדש. A new משנה lays out the עולת העוף, which mistakes disqualify it, and how wrong intentions (שלא לשמה, outside its place, beyond its time) affect bird offerings. The amud ends partway through the list of cases where the מתיר was not offered according to its מצוה, and the ruling for those cases comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The circling was done empty-handed
steps.stepSummary: The end of an earlier statement: the כהן גדול circled the altar 'on foot', without the wine in his hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: The circling was done on foot.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a statement from before this section. It says the כהן גדול walked around the altar 'on foot', meaning empty-handed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'On foot' does not just mean walking. It means he was not yet carrying the wine. He was handed the wine only when he reached the corner where it would be poured.

keyTerms.meaning: Circling, going around the altar
On foot; here, empty-handed

phrases.english: The circling is on foot.
phrases.notes: 'On foot' here means with empty hands. He was not holding the wine yet while he walked around.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends a statement that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול circled the altar empty-handed and received the wine only at the corner where he poured it.

steps.title: רבא proves it from the wording of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out that the משנה says 'they give him wine to pour', not 'they tell him to pour'. So he was not holding the wine while he circled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The wording is also precise. The משנה says 'they give him wine to pour', and it does not say 'they tell him: pour.' Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא backs up the previous statement by looking closely at the exact words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כהן גדול were already holding the wine, the משנה would only need to say 'they tell him to pour.' Because it says 'they give him wine', he must have been handed the wine only at that moment. That means he circled empty-handed.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also precise; it supports this
They give him
To pour (a libation)
Learn from this; it is proven

steps.whatToRemember: The כהן גדול walked around the altar empty-handed. He received the wine only at the place where he poured it.

phrases.english: Rava said: It is also precise,
phrases.notes: He means the exact wording of the משנה supports what was just said.

phrases.english: since it teaches 'they give him wine to pour,'
and it does not teach 'one says to him: pour';
learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 1 from the wording of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That the circling was done empty-handed
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's wording 'they give him wine to pour' rather than 'they tell him to pour'

steps.title: A ברייתא on which side of the ramp to go up and come down
steps.stepSummary: Normally a person goes up the ramp on the right (east) side and comes down on the left (west) side. For three special services, he goes up and comes down on the west side, which the ברייתא calls 'right.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Everyone who goes up to the altar goes up on the right and comes down on the left. They go up on the east and come down on the west. The exception is someone who goes up for these three things: he goes up on the west and comes down on the west, and he goes up on the right and comes down on the right.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, a ברייתא, about which side of the ramp people use. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ramp is on the south side of the altar. A person walking up it faces north, so east is on his right and west is on his left. The general rule is: up on the east (right), down on the west (left). For three special services, he goes up and down on the west, but the ברייתא describes this as 'right.'

keyTerms.meaning: They go up
They come down
By way of the right side
East / west

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: All who go up to the altar –

phrases.aramaic: עוֹלִין דֶּרֶךְ יָמִין וְיוֹרְדִין דֶּרֶךְ שְׂמֹאל,
phrases.english: go up by way of the right and come down by way of the left,

phrases.aramaic: עוֹלִין דֶּרֶךְ מִזְרָח וְיוֹרְדִין דֶּרֶךְ מַעֲרָב;
phrases.english: they go up by way of the east and come down by way of the west;

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ מִן הָעוֹלֶה לִשְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים הַלָּלוּ –
phrases.english: except for one who goes up for these three things –
phrases.notes: The three are the wine libation, the water libation, and the bird עולה.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁעוֹלִים דֶּרֶךְ מַעֲרָב וְיוֹרְדִין דֶּרֶךְ מַעֲרָב,
phrases.english: who go up by way of the west and come down by way of the west,

phrases.aramaic: עוֹלִין דֶּרֶךְ יָמִין וְיוֹרְדִין דֶּרֶךְ יָמִין.
phrases.english: they go up by way of the right and come down by way of the right.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the paths on the ramp.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Normally a person goes up on the east and comes down on the west. For the three special services, he goes up and comes down on the west side.

steps.title: The west side should be called left, not right
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: for someone walking up the ramp, the west side is on his left, so how can the ברייתא call it 'right'?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'By way of the right'?! It is by way of the left!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spots a problem in the last line of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the ברייתא already said that west is 'left.' So the exception clause, which says 'west' and then calls it 'right,' contradicts the first half.

keyTerms.meaning: It is by way of the left!

phrases.english: 'By way of the right'?!
It is by way of the left!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the exception clause in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The exception clause of the ברייתא, which calls the west side 'right'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's own first half calls west 'left,' so calling the same side 'right' contradicts it.

steps.title: רבינא: change the word to 'left'
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers by correcting the ברייתא so that it says 'left.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Read it as 'left.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא solves the problem by fixing the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבינא, the word 'right' in the exception clause is simply a mistake. It should say 'left,' which matches the west side.

phrases.english: Ravina said: Teach 'left.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא really says 'right' for the west side.

steps.title: רבא: the altar's right versus the person's left
steps.stepSummary: רבא keeps the wording. 'Right' in the exception means the altar's right, and 'left' in the first half means the person's left.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is 'right'? The right of the altar. And what is 'left'? The left of the person.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer that does not change any words. He explains that the ברייתא is speaking from two different viewpoints.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you picture the altar as facing south, its right side is the west. For a person walking up the ramp, the west is on his left. So both words describe the same west side, seen from two different viewpoints.

keyTerms.meaning: The altar's right side
The person's left side

steps.confusionAlert: Both 'right' and 'left' here point to the same west side. They only sound like opposites because one is said from the altar's view and the other from the person's view.

phrases.english: Rava said: What is 'right'?
The right of the altar,
and what is 'left'? The left of the person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the קשיא in step 4, different from רבינא's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the words without changing them
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Right' and 'left' are said from the same viewpoint, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Right' is from the altar's viewpoint, and 'left' is from the person's viewpoint.

steps.title: Why would the ברייתא mix two viewpoints?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: the ברייתא should have used one viewpoint for both halves, either the altar's or the person's.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let it teach both from the altar's viewpoint, or both from the person's viewpoint!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is strange for one ברייתא to switch viewpoints partway through without saying so. A consistent text would use the same viewpoint the whole time.

keyTerms.meaning: But let it teach
This one and that one; both

phrases.english: But let it teach either both of them from the altar's view,
or both of them from the person's view!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's answer in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's explanation that the ברייתא uses two different viewpoints
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single ברייתא would not switch between the altar's viewpoint and the person's viewpoint; it would stay consistent.

steps.title: The difficulty stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that the question against רבא has no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends this discussion by admitting that רבא's explanation remains difficult.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question about mixing viewpoints is left without an answer. רבינא's simpler approach of changing the wording is not challenged here.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; the question stands without an answer

steps.whatToRemember: The exception clause seems to call the west side 'right.' רבינא fixes the text to read 'left.' רבא explains it as the altar's right, but his answer is left with an unanswered קשיא.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Admits that the challenge in step 7 is not answered.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא's two-viewpoint explanation remains difficult, while רבינא's corrected wording stands unchallenged.

steps.title: How the bird sin offering is performed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the steps of the חטאת העוף: מליקה without separating the head, sprinkling on the wall of the מזבח, squeezing the rest onto the יסוד, and the meat going to the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: How was the bird sin offering done? The כהן would pinch off its head from the back of the neck without separating it. He would sprinkle some of its blood on the wall of the altar, and squeeze the rest of the blood out onto the base. The altar gets only its blood, and the whole bird goes to the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins and describes, step by step, how a חטאת העוף is offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two blood steps: first sprinkling on the wall of the מזבח, then squeezing out the leftover blood onto the יסוד. Unlike a bird עולה, nothing of this bird is burned on the מזבח. Only the blood goes there, and the meat is eaten by the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird brought as a sin offering
Pinches the neck with the thumbnail (the way a bird offering is killed)
Its nape, the back of its neck
He does not separate the head from the body
Is squeezed out or drained
The base of the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the bird עולה. For the חטאת העוף the head stays attached, and the bird is eaten by the כהנים instead of being burned on the מזבח.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ חַטַּאת הָעוֹף כֵּיצַד הָיָה נַעֲשֵׂית?
phrases.english: MISHNA: The bird sin offering, how was it performed?
(He went up the ramp and turned to the surrounding ledge,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets, which describe where the כהן stood.

phrases.english: and came to the southeastern corner),

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה מוֹלֵק אֶת רֹאשָׁהּ מִמּוּל עׇרְפָּה
phrases.english: he would pinch off its head from opposite its nape
and does not separate it,
and sprinkles from its blood on the wall of the altar.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁיָרֵי הַדָּם הָיָה מִתְמַצֶּה עַל הַיְסוֹד;
phrases.english: The remaining blood would be squeezed out onto the base;
and the altar has only its blood,
and all of it goes to the priests.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ חַטַּאת הָעוֹף כֵּיצַד הָיָה נַעֲשֵׂית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the previous discussion ended with no answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a חטאת העוף the כהן does מליקה without separating the head, sprinkles the blood on the wall of the מזבח, and squeezes the rest onto the יסוד. Only the blood goes on the מזבח, and the meat goes to the כהנים.

steps.title: Blood is sprinkled straight from the body onto the lower wall
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from 'of the blood of the sin offering' that the blood is sprinkled directly from the bird's body. It must go on the wall of the מזבח, not on other walls, and that wall is the lower one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'And he shall sprinkle of the blood of the sin offering' means straight from the body of the sin offering. How? He holds the head and the body and sprinkles onto the wall of the altar. He does not sprinkle on the wall of the ramp, the היכל, or the אולם. Which wall of the altar? The lower wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains the משנה's sprinkling step from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'מדם החטאת' (of the blood of the sin offering) are read as 'from the body of the sin offering itself.' So the כהן uses no finger and no bowl; he holds the bird and sprinkles directly from it. The ברייתא also limits where the blood may go: only the מזבח's wall, and specifically the lower part.

keyTerms.meaning: Directly from the body of the sin offering
The wall of the ramp leading up to the מזבח
The Sanctuary building
The Entrance Hall in front of the היכל
The lower wall of the מזבח (below the red line)

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
"And he shall sprinkle of the blood of the sin offering" —
from the body of the sin offering.
How so?
He holds the head and the body,
and sprinkles on the wall of the altar;
and not on the wall of the ramp,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עַל קִיר הֵיכָל, וְלֹא עַל קִיר אוּלָם.
phrases.english: and not on the wall of the Sanctuary, and not on the wall of the Entrance Hall.
And which one? This is the lower wall.
phrases.notes: The 'lower wall' is the part of the מזבח below the red line that runs around its middle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source and details for the משנה's instruction to sprinkle on the wall of the מזבח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blood is sprinkled directly from the bird's body onto the lower wall of the מזבח, and not onto any other wall.

steps.title: Suggesting the upper wall by a logical argument
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests a קל וחומר: an animal חטאת goes higher than an animal עולה, and a bird עולה already goes on top, so a bird חטאת should go on top too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe it means only the upper wall? It makes logical sense: an animal's עולה goes below, yet its חטאת goes above. A bird's עולה already goes above, so shouldn't its חטאת surely go above?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own answer of 'lower wall' with a logical argument for the upper wall. This sets up the next move, where a פסוק will answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument works like this: in animals, the חטאת is placed higher than the עולה. A bird עולה already goes on the upper wall, so a bird חטאת should at least go there too. This attacks the claim from the previous step that the bird חטאת goes on the lower wall.

keyTerms.meaning: The upper wall of the מזבח (above the red line)
'And it is logical,' introducing a reasoned argument
'Just as / if,' the opening word of a קל וחומר
Burnt offering
Below / above (the red line)

phrases.english: Or is it only the upper wall?
And it is logical:
Just as an animal, whose burnt offering is below —
its sin offering is above;
a bird, whose burnt offering is above —
is it not logical that its sin offering is above?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'lower wall' ruling of the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the bird חטאת's blood goes on the lower wall.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from animal offerings: since the חטאת goes above the עולה in animals, and the bird עולה is already above, the bird חטאת should be above as well.

steps.title: The verse proves it is the lower wall
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'the rest of the blood shall be squeezed out at the base of the altar' shows that the blood goes on a wall whose leftovers drain down to the יסוד. That is the lower wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And the rest of the blood shall be squeezed out at the base of the altar.' This means a wall whose leftover blood drains down to the base. Which wall is that? The lower wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the logical argument with a פסוק, which settles that the blood goes on the lower wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links the sprinkling to blood that drains down to the יסוד. Blood sprinkled high up would not drip straight down to the base, because the סובב (ledge) sticks out and gets in the way. So the פסוק overrides the קל וחומר and confirms the lower wall.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The verse teaches,' bringing a פסוק to decide the question
The rest of the blood
Shall be squeezed out
Leftovers (of the blood)

steps.whatToRemember: The blood of a חטאת העוף is sprinkled straight from the bird onto the lower wall of the מזבח. The proof is that its leftover blood has to drain to the יסוד, which only happens from the lower wall.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a classic pattern: a logical קל וחומר can be overruled when a פסוק teaches otherwise. That is why the bird חטאת is different from the animal חטאת here.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"And the rest of the blood shall be squeezed out at the base of the altar" —
a wall whose leftovers drain to the base;
And which one? This is the lower wall.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: וְהַנִּשְׁאָר בַּדָּם יִמָּצֵה אֶל יְסוֹד הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of the previous step with a פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק overrides the logical argument.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: By קל וחומר from animal offerings, the bird חטאת should go on the upper wall.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק ties the sprinkling to blood draining to the יסוד, which means the lower wall.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The חטאת העוף is sprinkled on the lower wall of the מזבח.

steps.title: Why not sprinkle above and then squeeze below?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 12: the כהן could sprinkle on the upper wall to satisfy the קל וחומר, and then squeeze the rest at the bottom to satisfy the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him sprinkle above, and afterwards squeeze below!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 12. It suggests a way to do both things: sprinkle high, then squeeze the leftover blood down at the יסוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 used 'squeezed out at the יסוד' to prove the sprinkling must be on the lower wall. The challenge says the פסוק only requires the leftovers to reach the יסוד. That could happen as a second, separate action after sprinkling on the upper wall, so the קל וחומר from step 11 would still stand.

keyTerms.meaning: From above (the upper part of the מזבח wall)
From below (the lower part, near the יסוד)
And then, afterwards

phrases.english: But let him do it above,
phrases.notes: He means sprinkling the blood on the upper half of the מזבח wall, like the קל וחומר wanted.

phrases.english: and then do it below!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof from the פסוק given in step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof in step 12 that the sprinkling must be on the lower wall
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק could be fulfilled by a separate squeezing at the bottom after sprinkling at the top, so it does not force the sprinkling itself to be low.

steps.title: The blood must drip down by itself
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the פסוק says 'יִמָּצֵה' (it shall be squeezed out, passive), not 'יְמַצֶּה' (he shall squeeze), so the blood must drain down on its own from where it was sprinkled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Is it written 'he shall squeeze out'? It is written 'it shall be squeezed out', which means it happens by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge from the exact wording of the פסוק. The verb is passive, so no one squeezes the blood down in a second act. It drips down by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the leftover blood has to reach the יסוד on its own, the sprinkling must be on a spot it can drip down from. That spot is the lower wall, right above the יסוד. So 'sprinkle above, then squeeze below' does not work, and the lower-wall rule from step 12 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall squeeze out (active, a person does it)
It shall be squeezed out / drained (passive, it happens on its own)
By itself, automatically

steps.whatToRemember: The blood of a bird חטאת goes on the lower wall, because the פסוק says the rest of the blood 'יִמָּצֵה' and drains to the יסוד by itself.
steps.confusionAlert: The two words are spelled with exactly the same letters (ימצה). The whole answer depends on the vowels: יְמַצֶּה means a person squeezes, while יִמָּצֵה means the blood drains on its own.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Is it written "he shall squeeze out"?!
It is written "it shall be squeezed out,"
which means by itself.
phrases.notes: The blood has to trickle down to the יסוד on its own, so it must be sprinkled low enough to do that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the verb form in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The squeezing could be a separate active step done after sprinkling high.
steps.terutzMaskana: The passive form 'יִמָּצֵה' means the blood drains by itself, so the sprinkling must be on the lower wall.

steps.title: How the כהן holds the bird for מליקה, according to רב
steps.stepSummary: רב describes how the כהן holds a bird חטאת: wings between two fingers, legs between two fingers, neck stretched across his thumb, and then he does מליקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זוטרא בר טוביה said in the name of רב: How do we do מליקה on a bird חטאת? He holds its wings with two fingers and its two legs with two fingers, stretches its neck across the width of his thumb, and does מליקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: the practical way the כהן does מליקה on a bird חטאת. רב gives a hand-by-hand description.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב's description the bird lies in the כהן's palm. Four fingers hold the wings and legs, and the neck rests across the thumb, so one hand both holds the bird and does the pinching.

keyTerms.meaning: Doing מליקה: cutting the bird's neck from the back with the thumbnail
Its wings
Stretches out
His thumb

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Zutra bar Toviyya said that Rav said:
How does one pinch the neck of a bird sin offering?
He holds its wings with two fingers
and the two legs with two fingers,
and stretches its neck across the width of his thumb,
and pinches it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב: כֵּיצַד מוֹלְקִין חַטַּאת הָעוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from where the blood goes to how the מליקה from the משנה in step 9 is physically done
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן holds the wings and legs with four fingers, stretches the neck over his thumb, and pinches.

steps.title: A ברייתא's different grip, and how hard this service is
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא describes the grip differently: the bird is on the outside of the hand, and the neck is stretched over two fingers. It adds that this is the hard service of the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: The bird is on the outside. He holds its wings with two fingers and its two legs with two fingers, stretches its neck across the width of his two fingers, and pinches. And this is the hard service in the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a slightly different way of holding the bird. The ברייתא also says this is the hard service in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two differences from רב: the bird sits on the back of the hand instead of in the palm, and the neck lies over two fingers instead of the thumb. The ending line, calling this 'the' hard service, sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
The bird is on the outside (back) of the hand
A difficult service

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
The bird is on the outside;
phrases.notes: The bird rests on the back of the כהן's hand, not inside his palm like in רב's version.

phrases.english: he holds its wings with two fingers
and the two legs with two fingers,

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹתֵחַ צַוָּארוֹ עַל רוֹחַב שְׁתֵּי אֶצְבְּעוֹתָיו,
phrases.english: and stretches its neck across the width of his two fingers,
and pinches.
And this is the difficult service in the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different description of the grip described in step 15
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bird is held on the outside of the hand with the neck stretched over two fingers, and this is called the hard service of the מקדש.

steps.title: Is מליקה the only hard service?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to the ברייתא calling מליקה 'the' hard service, since קמיצה and חפינה are also very hard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this the one, and no other? But there is also קמיצה and חפינה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the last line of the ברייתא. If מליקה is 'the' hard service, what about קמיצה and חפינה, which are also hard?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording 'זו עבודה קשה' sounds like only מליקה is hard. But קמיצה, taking a fistful from a מנחה, and חפינה, taking two handfuls of קטורת on יום הכיפורים, also need great skill. So the ברייתא's wording seems too strong.

keyTerms.meaning: And nothing else?
Taking a fistful from a מנחה
Scooping two handfuls of קטורת on יום הכיפורים

phrases.english: This is it, and nothing else?!
But there is also the taking of a fistful and the taking of handfuls!

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ הִיא – וְתוּ לָא?! וְהָאִיכָּא קְמִיצָה וַחֲפִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the closing line of the ברייתא in step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement 'וזו עבודה קשה שבמקדש'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קמיצה and חפינה are also hard services, so מליקה cannot be the only hard one.

steps.title: מליקה is one of the hard services
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords the ברייתא: מליקה is one of several hard services in the מקדש, not the only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: This is a hard service among the hard services in the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of the ברייתא so it no longer clashes with קמיצה and חפינה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of 'the hard service', read 'one of the hard services'. The ברייתא's point that מליקה is very difficult stays, and קמיצה and חפינה can be on the same list.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say (read the text this way)
From among the hard services

steps.whatToRemember: מליקה of a bird חטאת is one of the hardest services in the מקדש, together with קמיצה and חפינה.

phrases.english: Rather, say:

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ עֲבוֹדָה קָשָׁה מֵעֲבוֹדוֹת קָשׁוֹת שֶׁבַּמִּקְדָּשׁ.
phrases.english: This is a difficult service, one of the difficult services in the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: זוֹ עֲבוֹדָה קָשָׁה מֵעֲבוֹדוֹת קָשׁוֹת שֶׁבַּמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17 by rewording the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא meant מליקה is the single hard service.
steps.terutzMaskana: מליקה is one of several hard services, alongside קמיצה and חפינה.

steps.title: How the bird burnt offering begins: the head
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes the first stage of the עולת העוף. The כהן goes to the southeast corner, does the מליקה, separates the head, squeezes out the blood, salts the head and burns it.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is a bird burnt offering done? The כהן goes up the ramp, turns onto the ledge and comes to the southeast corner. He pinches off the head from the back of the neck, separates it fully, and squeezes the blood onto the wall of the מזבח. Then he takes the head, presses its cut end against the מזבח to squeeze out its blood too, salts it, and throws it onto the fire.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lays out step by step how the כהן starts bringing an עולת העוף, beginning with the head.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key actions are the מליקה from the back of the neck and fully separating the head from the body. Then come מיצוי הדם, squeezing the blood onto the wall. The head gets its own squeezing, salting and burning before the כהן moves on to the body.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird burnt offering
The ramp leading up to the מזבח
The ledge that runs around the מזבח
Pinches off with the thumbnail (doing מליקה)
Squeezed out (the blood)
The fires on top of the מזבח

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The bird burnt offering, how is it done?
He went up the ramp and turned to the ledge,
and came to the southeast corner.

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה מוֹלֵק אֶת רֹאשָׁהּ מִמּוּל עׇרְפָּה,
phrases.english: He would pinch off its head from opposite its nape,
and separate it, and squeeze out its blood
on the wall of the altar.
He took the head
and brought the place where it was pinched up against the altar,
soaked it up with salt,
and threw it onto the fires.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the גמרא's discussion of חטאת העוף and מליקה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עולת העוף is done at the southeast corner. The כהן does the מליקה, separates the head, squeezes out the blood, then salts the head and burns it.

steps.title: Preparing and burning the bird's body
steps.stepSummary: The כהן removes the crop, the feathers and the innards and throws them to the ash place. He rips the body open without separating it, salts it and burns it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he turns to the body. He removes the crop, the feathers and the innards that come out with them, and throws them to the ash place. He rips the body open but does not split it into two pieces. If he did split it, it is still valid. He salts it and throws it onto the fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the procedure, now dealing with the bird's body after the head is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The parts that are not burned are removed and thrown to בית הדשן. The ideal way is to tear the body open without splitting it into two halves. Even so, the משנה says splitting it does not make the קרבן פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: The crop, the food pouch in a bird's throat
The feathers (here, the ones attached to the crop)
The place where the ashes are put, near the מזבח
Ripped it open
Separated it into two pieces

phrases.english: He came to the body,
and removed the crop and the feathers
and the innards that come out with them,
and threw them to the place of the ashes.
He ripped it open, but did not separate it.
And if he separated it, it is valid.
He soaks it up with salt,
and throws it onto the fires.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the procedure from the head to the body.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The crop, feathers and innards are thrown to בית הדשן. The body is torn open, ideally without being split (though splitting is כשר), then salted and burned.

steps.title: Skipping steps after the blood is squeezed out
steps.stepSummary: If the כהן skipped removing the crop, the feathers or the innards, or skipped the salting, the קרבן is still כשרה. Any change made after מיצוי הדם does not ruin it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did not remove the crop, the feathers or the innards, and did not salt it, it is still valid. Any change he made after he squeezed out its blood does not disqualify it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now teaches which mistakes do not ruin the קרבן: anything done wrong after the blood was squeezed out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The squeezing of the blood is the main act. Once it is done properly, the later steps from steps 19-20, like removing parts and salting, are only the proper way to do things. Skipping them does not make the קרבן פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Changed (did differently from the proper way)
After he squeezed out (the blood)
Valid

steps.whatToRemember: For an עולת העוף, squeezing out the blood is the deciding act. Mistakes after that point do not disqualify it.

phrases.english: If he did not remove the crop nor the feathers
and the innards that come out with them,
and did not soak it up with salt –
anything that he changed in it
after he squeezed out its blood, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ideal procedure to which skipped steps still leave the קרבן valid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any change made after מיצוי הדם leaves the עולת העוף כשרה.

steps.title: Separating the head, and which blood must be squeezed
steps.stepSummary: Separating the head in a חטאת העוף, or not separating it in an עולת העוף, makes the קרבן פסול. Squeezing only the head's blood is פסול. Squeezing only the body's blood is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he separated the head in a sin offering, or did not separate it in a burnt offering, it is disqualified. If he squeezed out the blood of the head but not the blood of the body, it is disqualified. If he squeezed out the blood of the body but not the blood of the head, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives two rules that do decide whether the קרבן is valid: whether the head was separated, and which blood was squeezed out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עולה and the חטאת are opposites: the עולה must have its head separated, and the חטאת must not. For the blood, what counts is squeezing the body's blood. Squeezing only the head's blood is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Disqualified
The blood of the head
The blood of the body

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two birds: in the עולת העוף the head must be fully separated, but in the חטאת העוף it must not be.

phrases.english: If he separated the head in the sin offering
or did not separate it in the burnt offering – it is disqualified.
If he squeezed out the blood of the head
and did not squeeze out the blood of the body – it is disqualified.

phrases.aramaic: דַּם הַגּוּף וְלֹא מִיצָּה דַּם הָרֹאשׁ – כְּשֵׁירָה.
phrases.english: If he squeezed the blood of the body but not the blood of the head – it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After listing changes that do not matter, the משנה lists the ones that do.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wrong separating (in a חטאת or an עולה) disqualifies the קרבן. Only the body's blood squeezing is required.

steps.title: Bird offerings done for the wrong purpose
steps.stepSummary: A חטאת העוף whose מליקה or blood squeezing was done שלא לשמה, even only in part, is פסול. An עולת העוף done that way is כשרה, but it does not count for the owner's obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: A bird sin offering is disqualified if he pinched it not for its sake, or squeezed its blood not for its sake. This is true even if he did it first for its sake and then not, or first not and then for its sake. A bird burnt offering done this way is valid, but it does not count for the owner as his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with the rule for a bird קרבן done with the wrong intention, שלא לשמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a חטאת העוף, wrong intent at either the מליקה or the מיצוי ruins it, even if it was mixed with right intent. An עולת העוף stays a valid קרבן, but the owner still has to bring another one to fulfill his obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: Not for its own sake (for the wrong קרבן purpose)
The owners who brought the קרבן
As fulfilling the obligation

steps.whatToRemember: שלא לשמה: a חטאת העוף is פסול, while an עולת העוף is כשרה but does not fulfill the owner's obligation.

phrases.english: A bird sin offering that he pinched not for its sake;
or he squeezed out its blood not for its sake;
or for its sake and then not for its sake;
or not for its sake and then for its sake – it is disqualified.
A bird burnt offering is valid,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא עָלְתָה לִבְעָלִים לְשֵׁם חוֹבָה.
phrases.english: just that it does not count for the owner as his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from mistakes in physical actions to mistakes in intention.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חטאת העוף done שלא לשמה is פסול. An עולת העוף done שלא לשמה is כשרה but does not fulfill the owner's obligation.

steps.title: Wrong intentions of place and time in bird offerings
steps.stepSummary: An intention to eat or burn the bird outside its place makes it פסול without כרת. An intention to do so beyond its time makes it פיגול with כרת, provided the מתיר was offered according to its מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For both a חטאת העוף and an עולת העוף: if the כהן did the מליקה or squeezed out the blood while intending to eat what is normally eaten, or to burn what is normally burned, outside its proper place, the קרבן is פסול but there is no כרת. If he intended to do it beyond its proper time, it is פיגול and there is כרת, as long as the מתיר was offered according to its מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the basic rule for wrong intentions during the two main bird services, מליקה and squeezing the blood. It contrasts an intention about place with an intention about time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two kinds of wrong thoughts give two different results. A 'wrong place' thought only disqualifies the קרבן. A 'wrong time' thought makes it פיגול, which carries כרת for eating it, but only under one condition: the מתיר must have been done 'according to its מצוה.' The next steps explain that condition.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside its place: an intention to eat or burn the קרבן in the wrong location
Beyond its time: an intention to eat or burn the קרבן after its allowed time
A קרבן ruined by a 'beyond its time' intention; eating it carries כרת
Spiritual cutting off, the punishment for eating פיגול
The permitting factor: the service that makes the קרבן allowed

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the condition that runs through the rest of the משנה: a time-intention only creates פיגול if no place-intention spoils the מתיר.

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד חַטַּאת הָעוֹף וְאֶחָד עוֹלַת הָעוֹף,
phrases.english: Both a bird sin offering and a bird burnt offering,
where he pinched them or squeezed out their blood
intending to eat something that is normally eaten,
or to burn something that is normally burned
outside its place:
it is disqualified, and there is no כרת for it.
If beyond its time: it is פיגול,
and one is liable to כרת for it;
provided that the permitting factor was offered according to its מצוה.
phrases.notes: The 'permitting factor' here is the blood service, which is what makes the bird allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד חַטַּאת הָעוֹף וְאֶחָד עוֹלַת הָעוֹף, שֶׁמְּלָקָן וְשֶׁמִּיצָּה אֶת דָּמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the order of the bird services and intent of שלא לשמה to intentions of wrong place and wrong time.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A place-intention during מליקה or squeezing makes it פסול without כרת. A time-intention makes it פיגול with כרת, if the מתיר was offered according to its מצוה.

steps.title: Cases where the permitting factor is offered properly
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines 'according to its מצוה.' Silence in one service plus a time-intention in the other, or a time-intention in both, counts as proper, so the result is פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is the מתיר offered according to its מצוה? (1) He did the מליקה with no wrong thought and squeezed the blood with a 'beyond its time' thought. (2) He did the מליקה with a 'beyond its time' thought and squeezed the blood with no wrong thought. (3) He did both with a 'beyond its time' thought. These are cases where the מתיר was offered according to its מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains its condition from the last step by listing three cases that count as 'according to its מצוה.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In all three cases the only wrong thought is about time. Doing a service in silence, meaning with no wrong thought, does not spoil anything. So these cases are פיגול with כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: How? The משנה's way of introducing a definition
In silence: with no wrong thought at all
According to its מצוה: done without any other disqualifying thought mixed in
This is it: closes the list of examples

steps.confusionAlert: 'According to its מצוה' does not mean there was no bad thought at all. Even a time-intention in both services still counts as 'according to its מצוה.' It only means no other disqualifying thought, like a place-intention, was mixed in.

phrases.english: How is the permitting factor offered according to its מצוה?
He pinched in silence,
phrases.notes: 'In silence' means he had no wrong thought at all while doing it.

phrases.english: and squeezed out the blood with intent for beyond its time;
or he pinched with intent for beyond its time,
and squeezed out the blood in silence;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁמָּלַק וּמִיצָּה הַדָּם חוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ –
phrases.english: or he pinched and squeezed out the blood with intent for beyond its time:
this is where the permitting factor was offered according to its מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the condition 'provided that the מתיר was offered according to its מצוה' from step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Silence plus a time-intention, or a time-intention in both services, counts as the מתיר offered according to its מצוה, so it is פיגול.

steps.title: Cases where the permitting factor is not offered properly
steps.stepSummary: The משנה begins listing cases where a place-intention is mixed in, so the מתיר is not offered according to its מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is the מתיר not offered according to its מצוה? (1) He did the מליקה with an 'outside its place' thought and squeezed the blood with a 'beyond its time' thought. (2) He did the מליקה with a 'beyond its time' thought and squeezed the blood with an 'outside its place' thought. (3) He did both with an 'outside its place' thought.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists the opposite cases, where a place-intention spoils the מתיר. It is setting up a ruling about these cases that comes right after this list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each case a place-intention appears in at least one of the two services. That place-intention ruins the מתיר, so a time-intention in the other service cannot create פיגול. Cases (1) and (2) show that the order does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: Was not offered according to its מצוה: another disqualifying thought was mixed in
He did the מליקה, pinching the bird's neck with his fingernail
He squeezed out the blood

phrases.english: How is the permitting factor not offered according to its מצוה?
He pinched with intent for outside its place,
and squeezed out the blood with intent for beyond its time;
or he pinched with intent for beyond its time,
and squeezed out the blood with intent for outside its place;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁמָּלַק וּמִיצָּה הַדָּם חוּץ לִמְקוֹמוֹ;
phrases.english: or he pinched and squeezed out the blood with intent for outside its place;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite cases to step 25: here a place-intention is mixed in, so the מתיר is not according to its מצוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a place-intention appears in either service, the מתיר is not offered according to its מצוה. The ruling for these cases follows right after this list.
